name: Zach Top
notes: The 2024 neotraditional revival — "a deliberate 1990s reconstruction (Telecaster, steel, fiddle, two-beat) recorded with modern clarity." Keys are documented: "D major/D minor dominate his catalogue (a large block of album cuts read D or D minor), then G/E/C/B." Harmony is the entry's headline claim and is authored as its own vocabulary: "I–IV–V with V7, I–I7–IV blues turns, and i–iv–V on the minor cuts — the most pre-2000 harmonic vocabulary in the modern cohort," so the seventh share is high, the blues turn lives in the major_blues weighting and the minor family is i–iv–V rather than the modern i–VI–III–VII. Drums are "the default is a two-beat with quarter kick and hat opening on 4, plus cross-stick on the slow cuts," so the kick sits on all four beats with the open hat on beat 4 at the highest probability here. The bass is stated with two negatives that matter: "live electric or upright bass in staccato two-beat root-fifth; no programmed low end at all," so no `bass808` block and near-zero anticipation. The counter is the reconstruction's point — "pedal steel and fiddle as co-lead voices, acoustic bed, piano comping on the backbeat" — and the arrangement ends on a "tight stop-ending." Melody is "clear tenor with a country break, narrow verse range, chorus a fifth up, no melisma." ⚠ Boundary flag from the research: "a substantial part of this catalogue is honky-tonk shuffle and train-beat material — `country-shuffle` and `country-train` should claim those grooves outright." ⚠ Confidence is medium (research: medium-high); the per-track readings are [LOW-CONF] and the fast group's 172–188 figures fold to ~86–94. ⚠ The INFERRED parameters are the velocity tiers, the perc density and the counter ratio.
